My soul, how lovely is the place
'Tis heaven to see his smiling face,
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 84:1–4, 10, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts! 2My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. 3Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God. 4How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah 10For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
